newsitem.title: JAPAN: Manila's upgrading reflects improving economy-JCRA.
newsitem.headline: Manila's upgrading reflects improving economy-JCRA.

text.p: Japan Credit Rating Agency Ltd (JCRA) said on Wednesday its recent upgrading of the Philippines to investment grade reflected a significant improvement in its economic fundamentals.

"The major reason for the upgrading (of the Philippines) was a significant improvement in the country's economic fundamentals, such as growth, inflation and its budget balance," Yoshiyuki Nishimura, an analyst at JCRA, told Reuters Financial Television.
JCRA recently upgraded its rating for the Philippines to triple B (BBB), an investment grade rating, from triple B-minus (BBB-).

The Philippines has achieved over five percent annual growth in its gross national product (GNP) in real terms for the past three years, while inflation has declined to single-digit figures since 1992, Nishimura said.
For 1996, the public sector balance returned to surplus despite a decline in revenues due to the slowing down of the privatisation of state-run bodies.
The current account deficit has been at a manageable level of around four percent of GNP in the past three years, and the debt-servicing ratio has been improving, he said.
"In order to acquire a better rating, Manila needs to carry out the planned reform of corporate and income taxes, and reduce external debt further," Nishimura said.

Asked about a possible speculative attack on the Philippine peso in the future based on such negative factors as a rise in its trade deficit, Nishimura said, "The chance is unlikely to be significant."

Manila's economic structural reform has been progressing steadily amid the stable political climate, while the country has been steadily accumulating external reserves and managing external positions in a good manner.
Two international credit rating agencies, Standard & Poor's and Moody's Investors Service, upgraded their rating of the Philippines to one notch below investment grade earlier this year.
